title: Weekly links September 11: the fragility of high growth firms, women’s work and families, how many papers use AI now to write, and more…
gist: A links roundup whose two sharpest items are that high-growth firms are mostly 'one-hit wonders' — half exit within three to six years and fewer than 15% repeat — and that roughly 50% of economics arXiv papers and 25% of NBER working papers now contain at least one AI-classified 300-word window, with the acceleration starting only in 2025 alongside agentic coding tools.

themes.theme: Firm growth is luck, not persistent capability

insights.claim: Research on 'innovation bursts' finds that firms rapidly expand product portfolio, sales and employment through rare, outsized bursts even when they start small, and that among firms initially producing a single product, all product innovation comes from just 7% of them.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: If growth is burst-driven and concentrated in a tiny minority, portfolio approaches beat picking incumbents in small-cap and venture allocation.
insights.quote: of these firms, all product innovation comes from just 7% of them
insights.locator: High-growth happens only for short periods

insights.claim: If firms mainly expand through rare bursts, differences in firm size may reflect the luck of drawing a burst rather than persistent differences in innovative ability — which sits uneasily with the policy assumption that large firms are large because they innovate well.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Undermines the case for national-champion industrial policy and for paying up for 'proven innovators' on size alone.
insights.quote: differences in firm size may reflect the luck of drawing one of those bursts rather than persistent differences in the ability to innovate
insights.locator: High-growth happens only for short periods

insights.claim: World Bank research on high-growth firms finds as many as 50 percent of firms that experienced a high-growth event in the previous three years exit the market altogether within the following three to six years, while fewer than 15 percent repeat a high-growth episode.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Hard base rates for extrapolating a growth spurt: the modal outcome after a high-growth episode is exit, not repetition.
insights.quote: As many as 50 percent of firms that experienced a high-growth event in the previous three years are likely to exit the market altogether in the following three to six years
insights.locator: This is consistent with the high growth firms report

themes.theme: AI has captured academic writing since 2025

insights.claim: A classification of every NBER working paper and economics arXiv paper from January 2022 to mid-August 2026 using Pangram found almost none of the 2022 papers flagged as AI-written, which the analyst says shifted his priors on how well false positives can be avoided.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: A clean pre-LLM control period makes AI-detection statistics on academic text unusually credible.
insights.locator: Are papers now written with AI?

insights.claim: Roughly 50% of economics arXiv papers and about 25% of NBER working papers now have at least one 300-word window classified as AI-generated.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Signals how fast professional knowledge work has absorbed generative AI, and a coming credibility/disclosure problem for research-based decision inputs.
insights.quote: almost 50% of arXiv papers have at least one 300 word window classified as AI, and roughly 25% of NBER working papers
insights.locator: Are papers now written with AI?

insights.claim: The acceleration in AI-written paper sections began only in 2025 and coincides with the growth of agentic AI such as Claude Code rather than web-based platforms like ChatGPT.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Agentic tooling, not chat interfaces, is the adoption inflection for serious knowledge work — relevant to which AI products capture professional spend.
insights.quote: This acceleration coincides with the growth of agentic AI (Claude Code) rather than just web-based AI platforms like ChatGPT
insights.locator: Are papers now written with AI?

insights.claim: The classification exercise cost roughly three thousand dollars in API credits to run over the full NBER and economics arXiv corpus, chunking text and focusing on the introduction plus one randomly selected body section.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Corpus-scale LLM classification of an entire academic literature is now a low-four-figure project, which collapses the cost of this kind of audit.
insights.locator: I spent roughly three thousand dollars in API credits

insights.claim: On covariate selection for Callaway and Sant'Anna difference-in-differences, the relevant covariates are those that cause trends in the untreated potential outcome to differ and that are imbalanced, not those that merely shift outcome levels.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: A concrete rule for auditing DiD-based evidence before acting on it.
insights.quote: we don’t care about covariates that cause levels in the outcome to differ…we care about covariates that cause trends in the untreated potential outcome to be different
insights.locator: Do I need covariates for my DiD?

insights.claim: The AEA is launching a three-year randomized controlled trial that randomizes whether manuscripts go to referees with or without author names, and a 1991 trial found acceptance rates were lower and referees more critical when the reviewer did not know the author's identity.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: An institution running an RCT on its own gatekeeping process; the 1991 prior suggests double-blinding tightens acceptance rates.
insights.locator: You will be in a RCT if you submit to these journals

themes.theme: Women's work and the norms policy cannot reach

insights.claim: Legal change can expand women's ability to work, as Saudi Arabia shows, but social norms about who does specific household tasks are a deeper constraint and sit outside the traditional policy sphere for governments.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Caps the expected labor-supply response to legal reform in low-female-participation markets; norms move slower than statutes.
insights.quote: it’s not something that is really in the traditional policy sphere for governments
insights.locator: The consequences of more women working
